findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with ===, zero-length override check never matches
findings.body: `dayjs(...) === dayjs(...)` compares two distinct object references, so it is always false. A date override where start equals end (a day marked unavailable) is therefore not caught by this branch. Use `.isSame()` instead.

findings.title: Working hours end check uses slot start instead of slot end
findings.body: `end` is computed from `slotStartTime`, so it is identical to `start`. The `end > workingHour.endTime` check never accounts for the event length, and slots that run past the end of working hours are accepted. It should be computed from `slotEndTime`.

findings.title: Any non-matching working-hours entry marks the slot unavailable
findings.body: `workingHours.find` returns true as soon as one working-hours entry covering that weekday excludes the slot. Users with several ranges on the same day (e.g. 9-12 and 13-17) will have every slot rejected, because each slot falls outside at least one of the ranges. The check should be "not inside any entry" rather than "outside some entry".

findings.title: Slot that ends past the override end is still allowed
findings.body: Only `slotStartTime.isAfter(override end)` is rejected. A slot that starts inside the override but ends after the override end passes this check. Combined with the early `return true` when an override exists, this skips the busy-time checks and can produce bookable slots that overrun the override window.

findings.title: Override existence skips busy/booking checks
findings.body: When a slot falls on a day with a date override and inside it, the function returns true before evaluating `busy`. As a result, existing bookings and calendar events on override days are ignored, which allows double bookings.

findings.title: Date-override day matching shifts by the negated offset and compares in UTC
findings.body: The override start is shifted by the negative organizer UTC offset, but the slot's day is compared in UTC. Overrides near midnight in non-UTC zones are matched to the wrong day, so they can be applied to, or missed on, adjacent days.
